mainTopic: How far back a woman's טומאה reaches once she finds blood: שמאי, הלל, and the חכמים argue about retroactive impurity for the טהרות she touched.
overview: The first משנה of מסכת נדה asks a practical question. A woman finds menstrual blood. Do we worry that the blood actually started earlier, so that the pure items (טהרות) she touched before noticing are now impure? שמאי says no: her טומאה starts only from the moment she sees. הלל says it goes all the way back to her last self-check (פקידה), even many days back. The חכמים take a middle path: she goes back 24 hours (מעת לעת) or back to her last check, whichever is shorter. A woman with a fixed cycle (וסת) gets the rule that her time is enough, and checking with cloths at intercourse counts as a פקידה. The משנה gives a case showing what 'her time is enough' means, and it adds that the 24-hour look-back affects only טהרות, not when she starts counting her days. The גמרא then explains that שמאי relies on חזקה, the rule that a woman stays in her status of being pure. It begins to give הלל's answer: חזקה does not work where the weakness comes from the thing itself. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמאי: A woman's impurity starts only when she sees
steps.stepSummary: שמאי rules that women are impure only from the moment they find blood, with no backward reach.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: שמאי says: For all women, their time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with שמאי's view: when a woman finds blood, her טומאה starts right then, not earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry here is that the blood we find now, in the בית החיצון (the outer chamber of the womb), may have pooled there earlier too, held in by the walls of the womb, and she would have found it if she had checked. That would make everything she touched in between impure. שמאי declines to worry about that possibility; the Gemara later grounds his ruling in חזקה (step 9). Her impurity starts only from the moment she sees blood, and anything she touched before stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the start of the משנה text
'Her time is enough': her impurity begins only from the moment she sees blood
Retroactively, going backward in time (the idea the whole משנה is arguing about)

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה is about טהרות, pure food and items she touched. It is not about the laws of marital separation.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Shammai says:
All women, their time is enough.
phrases.notes: Meaning the moment she sees the blood is when her impurity starts. Nothing she touched before then becomes impure.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who sees blood is impure only from that moment; there is no retroactive טומאה.

steps.title: הלל: Impurity reaches back to her last check
steps.stepSummary: הלל rules that her טומאה goes back to the last time she checked and was clean, even if that was many days ago.
steps.simpleTranslation: הלל says: from check to check, and even if that is many days.
steps.whatsHappening: הלל gives the strict opposite of שמאי: her impurity reaches back to her last clean self-check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הלל, the only time we can be sure she was pure is the last time she actually checked. So everything she touched after that check becomes impure, no matter how long ago the check was.

keyTerms.meaning: A self-examination to see whether there is blood
From one check to the next: impurity goes back to the last clean check

phrases.english: Hillel says: From examination to examination,
and even for many days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with שמאי, taking the strict opposite view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her טומאה goes back to her last clean פקידה, however many days ago that was.

steps.title: The חכמים: 24 hours or the last check, whichever is shorter
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject both views. She goes back either 24 hours or to her last check, whichever is less time.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: not like this one and not like that one. Rather, a 24-hour period cuts down the time from check to check, and the time from check to check cuts down the 24-hour period.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a middle position between שמאי and הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her last check was more than a day ago, she only goes back 24 hours, not all the way to the check. If she checked within the last day, she only goes back to that check, not a full 24 hours. Either way, she uses whichever period is shorter.

keyTerms.meaning: From time to time: a full 24-hour period
Reduces or cuts down (the amount of retroactive time)

steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions: שמאי says only from now. הלל says back to the last check. The חכמים say the shorter of 24 hours or back to the last check.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: Not like the words of this one,
and not like the words of that one,
rather, a twenty-four-hour period reduces
the time from examination to examination,
phrases.notes: So if her last check was more than a day ago, she only worries about the last 24 hours.

phrases.english: and from examination to examination reduces
the twenty-four-hour period.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects both שמאי and הלל and offers a compromise
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Retroactive טומאה lasts for whichever is shorter: 24 hours or the time since her last clean פקידה.

steps.title: A woman with a fixed cycle, and checking with cloths
steps.stepSummary: A woman with a וסת is impure only from when she sees. Checking with cloths at intercourse counts as a פקידה and shortens the retroactive time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any woman who has a fixed cycle, her time is enough. And one who has intercourse using examination cloths, this counts like a check, and it reduces the 24-hour period and reduces the time from check to check.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two special cases to the חכמים' rule: a woman with a regular cycle, and a woman who checks with cloths at intercourse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman with a וסת sees blood at its expected time, so we do not suspect it came earlier. She gets שמאי's lenient rule. Checking with cloths before and after intercourse counts as a real check. That clean check becomes the new starting point, which cuts down both the 24-hour period and the time back to her previous check.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, predictable menstrual cycle
Has intercourse while using examination cloths to check for blood
Examination cloths (literally 'witnesses')

steps.confusionAlert: Even the חכמים agree with שמאי's leniency here, but only for a woman with a fixed וסת. This is a special case, not a reversal of their main rule.

phrases.english: Any woman who has a fixed cycle —
her time is enough,
and one who has intercourse with examination cloths —
this is like an examination,
and it reduces the twenty-four-hour period
and the time from examination to examination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds special cases that refine the חכמים' rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman with a וסת has no retroactive טומאה; checking with cloths counts as a פקידה and shortens the retroactive window.

steps.title: What does 'her time is enough' look like?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks for a concrete example of דיה שעתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does 'her time is enough' work?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question to set up a practical example of the phrase 'her time is enough.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the phrase was abstract. Here the משנה asks how it plays out in real life, and the next step answers with a case.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? A request for a practical example

phrases.english: Her time is sufficient, how so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a practical example of the rule just stated
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case showing what דיה שעתה means

steps.title: The case: she is impure, but the items she handled stay pure
steps.stepSummary: A woman handling טהרות in bed gets up and finds blood. She is impure, but the items she handled remain pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: She was sitting in bed and busy with pure items. She got up and saw blood. She is impure, and the items are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question with a case that shows דיה שעתה in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She was touching טהרות right up until she noticed the blood. Since her טומאה starts only when she sees, we do not say the blood began while she was handling them. So the items stay pure even though she herself is now impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually pure food or items that must be guarded from טומאה
She left or got up (from the bed)
Ritually impure (feminine)

steps.whatToRemember: דיה שעתה means the טהרות she touched before seeing the blood stay pure. Only from the moment of seeing is she impure.

phrases.english: If she was sitting in the bed
and busy handling pure items,
and she got up and saw blood —
she is impure and they are pure.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the pure items she was handling in bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the כיצד question with a case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A woman handling טהרות who gets up and finds blood is impure, but the טהרות remain pure.

steps.title: Her counting starts only from when she saw
steps.stepSummary: Even though the חכמים said she makes things impure going back 24 hours, she counts her days only from the moment she actually saw blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though the חכמים said she makes things impure for the 24 hours before she saw, she only starts counting her days from the moment she actually saw blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to the חכמים's rule of מעת לעת. Looking back in time only matters for the טהרות she touched. It does not move back the start of her counting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 24-hour look-back is a safety rule to protect pure food and items. It does not mean we treat her as if she really saw blood earlier. So her count of days begins from the real sighting.

keyTerms.meaning: From one time to the same time the day before, a full 24-hour period
She makes things impure (here, the טהרות she touched)
She counts (the days of her נדה period)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two rules. The 24-hour look-back affects only the items she touched. Her own count of days starts at the actual sighting.

phrases.english: Even though they said
she makes things impure for a 24-hour period back,
she does not count
except from the moment that she saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה with a limit on how far the retroactive rule reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Looking back 24 hours affects only טהרות. Her count of days begins at the actual sighting.

steps.title: What is שמאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why שמאי says she is impure only from the moment she sees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה. It asks why שמאי holds that a woman is impure only from when she sees blood, with no looking back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both הלל and the חכמים make her impure for some time before she saw. So the גמרא wants to know what lets שמאי ignore the earlier time completely.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
What is his reason?

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the reason of Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא after the משנה ends
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic behind שמאי's view that she is impure only from the moment she sees

steps.title: שמאי: a woman keeps her status of being pure
steps.stepSummary: שמאי relies on חזקה. Since the woman was pure, we assume she stayed pure until we know otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: leave the woman in her known status, and a woman is known to be pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמאי uses the rule of חזקה. We assume things stay the way they were until we know they changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before she saw blood, she had a clear status of being pure. Without proof that the blood came earlier, we keep her in that status. So her impurity starts only at the sighting.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this is his view)
A presumed status: we assume things stay as they were until proven otherwise
Leave her in her presumed status

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole מחלוקת turns on whether the rule of חזקה applies to a woman. הלל's answer, which begins next, attacks exactly this point.

phrases.english: He holds: Leave a woman in her presumed status,
and a woman stands in the presumed status of being pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about שמאי's reason
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמאי relies on חזקה: the woman was pure, so she stays pure until she actually sees.

steps.title: הלל: חזקה fails when the thing has its own weakness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about הלל and begins its answer. The rule of חזקה applies only where there is no weakness coming from the thing itself, but a woman has one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And הלל? When we say 'leave a thing in its known status,' that is where it has no weakness coming from itself. But a woman...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why הלל disagrees with שמאי and starts to answer. The answer is cut off here and continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל agrees that חזקה is a real rule, but he limits it. It works only when nothing inside the thing itself makes a change likely. A woman naturally sees blood, so her status of being pure is weaker. That is why הלל looks back to her last check.

keyTerms.meaning: A weakness or flaw that weakens a presumed status
From itself, coming from the thing's own nature
A woman (Aramaic)

steps.confusionAlert: הלל does not reject the rule of חזקה. He only says it doesn't fully protect a case like this, where the change can come from her own body.

phrases.english: And Hillel?
phrases.notes: Short for: and what is הלל's reason?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמַר: הַעֲמֵד דָּבָר עַל חֶזְקָתוֹ —
phrases.english: When one says: Leave a thing in its presumed status —
that is where it has no weakness coming from itself,
but a woman

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלֵּל? כִּי אָמַר: הַעֲמֵד דָּבָר עַל חֶזְקָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from שמאי's reason to הלל's, limiting the חזקה argument
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקה applies only where the thing has no weakness from itself. A woman does have such a weakness, and the explanation continues in the next section.
